cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: And in the mid nineteen nineties, I accidentally discovered how to wipe out a certain kind of traffic jam.
cues.zh: 在 20 世纪 90 年代中期，我无意中发现了一种消除某种交通拥堵的方法。

cues.en: I was bored, and this was on 520
cues.zh: 那时我很无聊，正开在 520 号公路

cues.en: going west towards the bridges where there's always a whole bunch of stop and go driving.
cues.zh: 向西开往大桥，那里总是走走停停。

cues.en: And I was trying to avoid hitting the brakes by driving at the average speed.
cues.zh: 我试图通过保持平均车速来避免踩刹车。

cues.en: So drive slow, so a big open spot opens up.
cues.zh: 所以开慢一点，前方就会腾出一大片空地。

cues.en: And then, just before I arrive at the stopped wave of cars, they all take off.
cues.zh: 然后，就在我到达停滞的车流前，它们刚好都开走了。

cues.en: And if I got it just right, I'd never have to hit the brakes at all. And one evening, I looked in the rearview mirror and could see all the headlights,
cues.zh: 如果时机刚刚好，我甚至根本不用踩刹车。一天晚上，我看了看后视镜，能看到所有的车灯，

cues.en: and I could see the stop and go waves of clots of cars behind me. But in my lane, they were totally uniform,
cues.zh: 能看到我身后那些走走停停的车流波浪。但在我的车道上，车流完全是匀速的，

cues.en: which I guess is pretty obvious in hindsight that I was eating traffic waves. Everybody behind me has no reason to be doing the stop and go driving.
cues.zh: 现在回想起来这似乎很明显，我当时在“吃掉”交通波。我身后的每个人都没有理由再走走停停了。

cues.en: So one single car for miles and miles was wiping out all of the stop and go driving in a single lane.
cues.zh: 于是，一辆车在漫长的道路上消除了单车道上所有的走走停停。

cues.en: But I kept trying to do that whenever there was any kind of stop and go wave by having a big empty space ahead of my car,
cues.zh: 后来每当遇到走走停停的车流时，我都试图通过在车头前方留出巨大的空隙来继续这样做，

cues.en: and then accidentally discovered
cues.zh: 然后我无意中又发现

cues.en: another kind of traffic jam that would break up ahead of me sometimes.
cues.zh: 另一种有时会在我前方散开的交通拥堵。

cues.en: Of course, it didn't always work, but if you have a big empty space
cues.zh: 当然，这并不总是奏效，但如果你留出巨大的空隙，

cues.en: and there's a jammed merge zone ahead of you,
cues.zh: 而你前方正好是一个拥堵的汇流区，

cues.en: the jam is often kept alive by a solid row of cars in the through lane who won't let anybody in. They pack themselves together.
cues.zh: 拥堵往往是由直行车道上紧密排列、不让任何人并线的一排汽车维持着的。它们把自己挤得严严实实。

cues.en: And then there's cheaters who run down to the end and force their way in, and nobody can really stop them. They'll just wait until they can get in between two people.
cues.zh: 然后还有些不守规矩的人会开到尽头强行加塞，大家也没辙。他们就等着插进两辆车中间。

cues.en: So the traffic jam is really caused by a fight. There might be just a tiny percentage of cheaters going down to the end and forcing their way in.
cues.zh: 所以交通堵塞其实是由争抢引起的。可能只有极少数人会开到尽头然后强行加塞。

cues.en: But if I let them in early,
cues.zh: 但如果我早点让他们进，

cues.en: they'll merge ahead of me, and then they're not racing down to the end to get in line and do the big fight.
cues.zh: 他们就会在我前面汇入，然后他们就不用冲到尽头去排队和别人激烈争抢了。

cues.en: And then there's no reason for the traffic jam, and everybody in the through lane just takes off.
cues.zh: 这样就不会产生交通堵塞，直行车道上的所有人都能畅通无阻了。

cues.en: So I saw that happen a couple of times and
cues.zh: 所以我看到过好几次这种情况，

cues.en: realized
cues.zh: 并且意识到

cues.en: single drivers can have huge effects
cues.zh: 单个司机也能产生巨大的影响，

cues.en: if they behave differently,
cues.zh: 只要他们改变行为，

cues.en: if you let people ahead of you.
cues.zh: 只要你让别人开到你前面。

cues.en: But why
cues.zh: 但为什么

cues.en: close-up gaps in the first place?
cues.zh: 一开始大家要缩小车距呢？

cues.en: Well, sometimes it's to to block out the cheaters, but more often, it's someone
cues.zh: 嗯，有时是为了挡住加塞的人，但更多时候是因为

cues.en: will get ahead of you if you leave a space.
cues.zh: 如果你留出空隙，就会有人加塞到你前面。

cues.en: And now you're one car length back, and you're a loser.
cues.zh: 然后你就会落后一个车身，你就成输家了。

cues.en: If you have a space ahead of you, maybe two or three or four cars get ahead of you, and and now you're you're you're slow. Your commute takes longer.
cues.zh: 如果你前方有空隙，可能会有两辆、三辆或四辆车插到你前面，然后你就会变慢。你的通勤时间就会变长。

cues.en: But if your commute takes, forty minutes,
cues.zh: 但如果你的通勤时间是四十分钟，

cues.en: one car is, like, one second of your commute.
cues.zh: 一辆车其实也就占你通勤时间的一秒钟。

cues.en: So, like, if you let 10 cars get ahead of you, your commute is ten seconds longer.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你让10辆车开到你前面，你的通勤时间也就多十秒钟。

cues.en: So letting cars ahead of you is insignificant.
cues.zh: 因此，让别的车开到你前面其实微不足道。

cues.en: It's it's like there isn't any race. You're not gonna lose no matter how many cars you let ahead of you.
cues.zh: 这就好像根本没有比赛一样。无论你让多少辆车开到你前面，你都不会输。

cues.en: And I was doing this all the time, letting people get in when they had to merge
cues.zh: 我一直这么做，让需要并线的人能进来

cues.en: and found that half the time,
cues.zh: 结果发现有一半的时候，

cues.en: they leave. They merge past,
cues.zh: 他们进来就走了。他们并线过去，

cues.en: so they didn't really want my space at all. They just wanted to get through the line of cars that wasn't letting anybody in,
cues.zh: 所以其实根本不需要我的空位。他们只是想穿过那条不让人进的车流，

cues.en: and mine was the only hole.
cues.zh: 而我的空位是唯一的缺口。

cues.en: Now ahead of you, you see a typical Seattle jam. We're south of the city going on I 5, and there's a left hand exit to the express lanes.
cues.zh: 现在你前方看到的是典型的西雅图拥堵。我们在城南的 I-5 公路上，有一个通往快速车道的左侧出口。

cues.en: And very often, this thing is packed with a a mile of stopped cars
cues.zh: 经常这里会堵上整整一英里的车

cues.en: because nobody can get into the solid packed line. Like, it's not a bank teller line where you can go backwards to get to the end.
cues.zh: 因为没人能挤进那密不透风的车流。这不像银行柜台排队，你还能往回走去队尾。

cues.en: So if you miss your chance, you can't get into the express lanes.
cues.zh: 所以一旦错过机会，就进不了快速车道了。

cues.en: And every once in a while, there'll be a cheater that'll force their way in, and that's what stops the whole row of cars.
cues.zh: 偶尔会有个加塞的人强行挤进去，结果整排车就全停住了。

cues.en: So if my hole is letting people in
cues.zh: 所以如果我的空位是让人进的

cues.en: and they've been trying to get in this long long line and finally they get to my hole, they don't have to cheat. They can go in.
cues.zh: 而他们已经在这条长龙里等了很久，终于到了我的空位，他们就不用加塞了。可以直接进去。

cues.en: And I think even the cheating is caused by the people closing up ranks
cues.zh: 我觉得连加塞都是因为大家把队封死造成的

cues.en: because if I'm driving along and I wanna merge into this exit lane and it's a solid packed wall of cars,
cues.zh: 因为如果我开着车想并进这个出口车道，而面前是一堵密不透风的车墙，

cues.en: well, I see them as idiots. They're all, like, greedy. They... They've got theirs and they're not gonna let anybody else in.
cues.zh: 那我就会觉得他们都是白痴。全都那么贪心。他们……他们已经占到了位置，就不让别人进。

cues.en: So then I am justified in cheating. Then I'm getting back at all of the
cues.zh: 那我就有理由加塞了。我这是在报复那些

cues.en: greedy idiots who form the solid wall of cars.
cues.zh: 贪心到组成一堵车墙的白痴们。

cues.en: But then if I'm in the line, I see anybody who wants in as a cheater,
cues.zh: 但要是我也在车流里，就会把想插队的人都看成作弊者，

cues.en: and it's just this this idiotic competitive thing where each side thinks the other side is evil, and a fight develops.
cues.zh: 这就是那种愚蠢的竞争心态，双方都觉得对方是恶人，于是就起了冲突。

cues.en: But just by having the big empty spot ahead of my car from habit,
cues.zh: 但仅仅是因为习惯性地在我车前留出一大块空当，

cues.en: I discussed... Discovered that this kind of jam often breaks up just because of one driver leaving a big spot.
cues.zh: 我讨论过……发现这种拥堵常常会散开，就是因为有一个司机留出了一大块空当。

cues.en: The big spot has other effects like if you have to merge and you've got a big spot ahead of you,
cues.zh: 这块大空当还有别的作用，比如你要并线时，如果前方有一大块空当，

cues.en: you have a lot of choices of who to get in between.
cues.zh: 你就有很多选择，可以插到谁和谁之间。

cues.en: Now if you have no no space ahead,
cues.zh: 可如果你前方没有空间，

cues.en: then you
cues.zh: 那你

cues.en: only have one chance. Either that or you have to slow down to drift along to find a slot.
cues.zh: 就只有一次机会。要么这样，要么你得减速慢慢滑行，去找一个空位。

cues.en: Oh oh, now here's the the jam. I've been letting people in ahead of me here to get in the
cues.zh: 哦哦，现在这里就是拥堵了。我一直在让别人插到我前面，好进入

cues.en: left hand exit lane.
cues.zh: 左侧出口车道。

cues.en: And I guess I didn't let enough in because here we're stopped.
cues.zh: 我猜我放进来的人还不够多，因为这里我们停住了。

cues.en: But the reason it stops is because people down at the far end are fighting,
cues.zh: 但停下来的原因是，最前面那头的人在争抢，

cues.en: and it makes them take turns and brings everything to a halt.
cues.zh: 这就逼得他们轮流走，把一切都弄停了。

cues.en: So two kinds of traffic jam that an individual driver can
cues.zh: 所以有两种交通拥堵，单个司机就能

cues.en: affect hugely,
cues.zh: 极大地影响，

cues.en: and that's these merging zone jams
cues.zh: 就是这些并线区的拥堵

cues.en: and the stop and go driving, the traffic waves that you can wipe out in your lane.
cues.zh: 以及走走停停的驾驶，那些交通波，你可以在自己车道里把它们消掉。

cues.en: There's a third effect,
cues.zh: 还有第三种效应，

cues.en: which is the effect on the driver that I used to be pushing and pushing and pushing through the traffic heavy congestion.
cues.zh: 就是对司机本人的影响，我以前总是在严重拥堵的车流里挤啊挤、挤啊挤。

cues.en: I was the type a that was gonna get, like, 10 cars ahead on my commute and and think that I done a big thing when it's... I've only gone ten seconds faster than everybody else.
cues.zh: 我以前是那种人，通勤路上能超前个十辆车，就觉得干了件大事，其实……我只比别人快了十秒钟。

cues.en: And now I'm like the zen warrior that knows how to shatter traffic jams as I approach them. Well, sometimes.
cues.zh: 现在我感觉自己就像个禅宗武士，在接近交通拥堵时知道如何将其化解。好吧，有时候是这样。

cues.en: But it's completely calm existence.
cues.zh: 但这完全是一种平静的存在。

cues.en: Now I'm I'm the philosopher that's helping helping everybody around me rather than the competitor that's screwing everybody and backstabbing right and left to get my my 10 feet
cues.zh: 现在的我，是一个在帮周围所有人解惑的哲学家，而不是那个为了向前挪动区区十英尺

cues.en: of traffic a couple of car lengths ahead.
cues.zh: 几个车身的距离，而在四处捅刀、算计所有人的竞争者。

cues.en: That's a totally different life as a commuter when you do it that way.
cues.zh: 当你用这种方式通勤时，那是完全不同的人生。
